questions.q: When must federal elections be held in Canada?
questions.a: On the third Monday in October every four years after the last general election
w: Every two years on July 1
Every five years on the first Monday in May
Whenever the Governor General wants
questions.e: Under the law, a federal election must be held on the third Monday in October every four years following the most recent general election. The Prime Minister may ask the Governor General to call an earlier election.

questions.q: The Prime Minister can ask the Governor General to call an election before the fixed date.
questions.e: Federal elections are held on a fixed date every four years, but the Prime Minister may advise the Governor General to call an earlier election.

questions.q: What is an electoral district (riding)?
questions.a: A geographical area represented by one Member of Parliament
w: A province with its own Senate
A city with its own mayor
A group of voters in the same party
questions.e: Canada is divided into electoral districts, also known as ridings or constituencies. An electoral district is a geographical area represented by a Member of Parliament (MP).

questions.q: How many federal electoral districts (ridings) are there in Canada today?
questions.e: Since the 2025 general election there are 343 electoral districts. Older copies of Discover Canada say 308, which was the number when the guide was written.

questions.q: In an electoral district, who becomes the Member of Parliament?
questions.a: The candidate who gets the most votes
w: The candidate chosen by the Prime Minister
The oldest candidate
The candidate who spends the most money
questions.e: The citizens in each electoral district elect one MP. The candidate who receives the most votes becomes the MP for that riding.

questions.q: Who can vote in a federal election?
questions.a: Canadian citizens who are at least 18 years old on voting day and are on the voters' list
w: All permanent residents aged 16 and over
Anyone who has lived in Canada for one year
Only people who own property
questions.e: To vote in a federal election you must be a Canadian citizen, be at least 18 years old on voting day and be on the voters' list.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to vote in a federal election?
questions.e: You must be at least 18 years old on voting day to vote in a federal election.

questions.q: Permanent residents can vote in federal elections.
questions.e: Only Canadian citizens aged 18 or older can vote in federal elections.

questions.q: Who maintains the National Register of Electors (the list of eligible voters)?
w: The Canada Revenue Agency
The RCMP
The Senate
questions.e: The voters' lists used in federal elections are produced from the National Register of Electors, a permanent database maintained by Elections Canada.

questions.q: Elections Canada is an independent, non-partisan agency.
questions.e: Elections Canada is an independent, non-partisan agency that runs federal elections and keeps the National Register of Electors.

questions.q: What does the voter information card tell you?
w: Who you should vote for
How much tax you owe
Your citizenship test result
questions.e: Once an election has been called, Elections Canada mails a voter information card to every elector on the list. It tells you when and where to vote.

questions.q: If you do not get a voter information card, what should you do?
questions.a: Contact Elections Canada to make sure you are on the voters' list
w: Do nothing because you cannot vote
Ask your employer to vote for you
Wait for the next election
questions.e: If you do not receive a voter information card, call your local elections office or Elections Canada to make sure you are on the voters' list.

questions.q: What is a secret ballot?
questions.a: Your vote is private and no one can watch you vote or see how you voted
w: A ballot that is counted by the Prime Minister
A vote that must be shown to your family
A ballot only for members of the armed forces
questions.e: Canadian law secures the right to a secret ballot. No one can watch you vote or look at how you voted. You may choose to discuss how you voted, but no one has the right to make you.

questions.q: Your employer has the right to ask you who you voted for.
questions.e: Voting is secret. No one, including your employer, has the right to insist that you tell them how you voted.

questions.q: If you cannot vote on election day, what can you do?
questions.a: Vote at an advance poll or by special ballot
w: Ask a friend to vote twice
Vote by phone the next week
Nothing, you lose your vote
questions.e: If you cannot or do not want to vote on election day, you can vote at advance polling days or by special ballot.

questions.q: On election day, what do you mark on the ballot?
questions.a: An X beside the name of the candidate of your choice
w: Your own name and address
The name of a political party leader you write in
A number for every candidate
questions.e: On election day, go to your polling station, mark your ballot with an X next to the candidate of your choice and put it in the ballot box.

questions.q: Canadian citizens have the right to be a candidate in an election.
questions.e: The right to vote and to be a candidate in elections is a democratic right of Canadian citizens.

questions.q: After an election, which party usually forms the government?
questions.a: The party with the most elected representatives
w: The party with the oldest leader
The party chosen by the Senate
The party that came second
questions.e: Usually, after an election, the leader of the political party with the most seats in the House of Commons is invited by the Governor General to form the government.

questions.q: Who becomes Prime Minister after an election?
questions.a: Usually the leader of the party with the most seats in the House of Commons
w: The candidate with the most votes in the whole country
The Governor General
The leader chosen by the Senate
questions.e: The leader of the party with the most seats is invited by the Governor General to form the government and becomes Prime Minister.

questions.q: What is a majority government?
questions.a: When the governing party holds at least half of the seats in the House of Commons
w: When the government has the support of most provinces
When the Prime Minister wins his or her own riding
When the Senate agrees with the government
questions.e: If the governing party holds at least half of the seats in the House of Commons, this is called a majority government.

questions.q: What is a minority government?
questions.a: When the governing party holds less than half of the seats in the House of Commons
w: When the government is run by the smallest party
When the Prime Minister is not elected
When fewer than half of people vote
questions.e: If the governing party holds less than half of the seats in the House of Commons, this is called a minority government.

questions.q: In a minority government, the government needs support from other parties to stay in power.
questions.e: A minority government needs the support of at least one other party to pass laws and win confidence votes in the House of Commons.

questions.q: The parties that are not in power are called what?
w: Cabinet parties
Royal parties
Senate parties
questions.e: The parties that are not in power are known as opposition parties. The one with the most members is the Official Opposition.

questions.q: Most Cabinet ministers are Members of Parliament.
questions.e: Cabinet ministers are chosen by the Prime Minister, usually from among the members of the House of Commons.

questions.q: Which of these elections can Canadian citizens vote in?
questions.a: Federal, provincial or territorial, and municipal elections
w: Only federal elections
Only municipal elections
Only elections in the province where they were born
questions.e: Canadian citizens can vote in federal, provincial or territorial, and municipal (local) elections.

questions.q: How do you learn about the candidates in an election?
questions.a: Through news, debates, candidates' websites and campaign materials
w: The government tells you who to vote for
Your employer chooses for you
Candidates are kept secret until election day
questions.e: Voters can learn about the candidates and parties through news, debates, websites and campaign material before deciding how to vote.

questions.q: Federal elections in Canada are usually held every four years.
questions.e: Federal elections are held on a fixed date every four years, unless an early election is called.

questions.q: Members of Parliament are appointed by the Prime Minister.
questions.e: MPs are elected by the voters in their electoral district. Senators, not MPs, are appointed.

questions.q: What do people in each electoral district elect in a federal election?
questions.a: One Member of Parliament for the House of Commons
w: The Prime Minister directly
A senator
A Lieutenant Governor
questions.e: Canadians do not vote directly for the Prime Minister. They elect one MP in their riding, and the leader of the party with the most seats usually becomes Prime Minister.

questions.q: In Canada, voters choose the Prime Minister directly with a separate vote.
questions.e: There is no separate vote for Prime Minister. The leader of the party with the most seats in the House of Commons usually becomes Prime Minister.

questions.q: You must tell the official at the polling station who you voted for.
questions.e: Voting is secret. No one can make you say how you voted.
